limitations: A cone equilibrium failure can be a contact orientation or solved-pose/COM problem; it is not proof no climbable beta exists.
Force-only diagnostic removes moment constraints but retains identical eight-ray cones; it uses recorded rounded contact data.
Unknown/infeasible must not be relabeled safe; approximate static support and proxy fatigue need setters validation.

evidence: boulderlab/draft_generation.py:generate_option stops mask/refinement stages at geometry pass
findings.finding: A geometry-passing route is returned before support diagnostics can affect installed geometry or beta choice. All six saved routes have geometry pass and static infeasible.

Roof-mounted hand-3 sloper working surface has y-axis about -0.759. With slope 0.6 its largest possible upward force component per unit axial force is still negative (about -0.369). Roof hand-4 pocket selected working envelope has y-axis about -0.758, slope0.65 and also no positive upward ray. These contact choices cannot support hanging upward; use a compatible declared grip or another installed location/geometry and independently check.

When remaining hand is sloper/pocket main, its axis z is about0.96 and feet z about0.72. Their cones can all point outward, making force balance impossible independently of COM or capacity. A foot position-only nudge cannot fix incompatible force directions.

Other failures retain force-only equilibrium but cannot cancel moments at the solved COM. Release poses typically inherit nearly the same COM as the preceding four-contact pose. Search should examine actual three-contact support before rewarding reach or short sequences; foot movement, hold orientation, and a different reachable body position can help.

Only three of the six routes have any capacity overload: roofB2.4810036, roofC1.3477135, overhangC1.0291336. All other failures are cone equilibrium; residual checks do not indicate numerical tolerance failure. Missing residuals on no-equilibrium states mean no reaction allocation found, not zero error.

beta_audit._search currently filters hand contacts to main (or explicit end), although declared alternate grip surfaces exist. Generator may compare explicit selected surfaces per placement, or extend independent search carefully; do not invent contact permission.
